title: Standardization of Goods Description in Customs Declarations
summary: The concept of 'description' evolved from a simple requirement for identifying goods in manual or basic electronic entries to a structured, mandatory component of regulatory compliance and audit trails. Over time, the legal framework shifted from general declarations to specific, standardized table-based reporting for tariff classification, duty assessment, and post-importation audit verification.

evolution.structure: Transitioned from free-form text to rigid, table-based HS-code-linked descriptions.
evolution.purpose: Expanded from basic identification to a critical data point for audit, tariff valuation, and post-clearance verification.
evolution.accountability: Increased responsibility on both importers and officials (EOs) to verify and document descriptions.

timeline.change: Initial establishment of structured tabular format for HS code and goods description.
Integration of description requirements into specific industrial import declarations (pre-fabricated buildings).
Refinement of description-based classification for Regulatory Duty (RD) application.
Formalization of description-linked tariff values for specific commodities.
Introduction of explicit procedural requirements for marking and describing goods by the Examining Officer (EO).

Customs Act 1969: This SRO is issued under the authority provided by Section 25(3) of the Customs Act 1969.
TABLE-1: This order amends the tariff values specified in Table-1 of the existing SRO for several specific goods identified by their H.S. Codes.
TABLE-2: This order replaces the entire Table-2 of the previous SRO with a new, comprehensive schedule that defines the minimum import values for a wide range of goods based on their H.S. Code, description, unit, and origin.
This instrument specifies amendments to entries within TABLE-2, modifying existing headings and H.S. Code listings to reflect updated classifications.
H.S. Code: Multiple H.S. Code entries within TABLE-2 are substituted with corrected versions for headings related to specific chemical compounds and chemical products.
A new heading and its corresponding H.S. Code and description are inserted into the table following the existing entries for a specific heading.

Customs Act 1969: Section 18, sub-section (2) of this Act empowers the Government to impose or adjust regulatory duties on imported goods.
The Act provides the legislative framework for the First Schedule, which classifies goods and determines import duty rates.
Import Duty: This order adjusts the rate of import duty to 3% for a wide range of goods that currently fall under the 25% statutory duty rate category, excluding specifically listed items or those exempted by other notifications and orders.
Regulatory Duty: This order imposes a specific regulatory duty on the commodities listed in Table-II, with rates ranging between 3% and 35% depending on the specific H.S. Code and product description.
First Schedule: The First Schedule of the Customs Act is the reference document for identifying H.S. Codes and the corresponding statutory import duty rates that are now subject to the amendments made by this order.
TABLE-I: This table lists specific goods, identified by H.S. Code and description, that are explicitly excluded from the 3% import duty adjustment established in this order.
